The necessary journey from the place of arrest to that magistrate’s court took four hours. Considering only this time-limit calculation, what is correct?

Counted time is 23 hours; the 24-hour limit is met on these facts.
Counted time is 31 hours; journey time must be added.
The Constitution allows 48 hours in every ordinary arrest.

question_snapshot.stem_en: In an ordinary arrest governed by Article 22(2), twenty-four hours have elapsed after excluding the necessary journey time. No magistrate has authorised further custody. The police seek to continue custody solely because the investigation is unfinished. Which conclusion follows?
options_en: An unfinished investigation automatically extends police custody by another twenty-four hours.
A superior police officer’s approval is sufficient in place of a magistrate’s authority.
The person must be acquitted because the production period has expired.
Further custody cannot be justified on that ground alone without a magistrate’s authority.
